# SEG Solar opens 4 GW Texas facility, announces plan to become the nation’s largest crystalline silicon module maker

Ben Zientara
SEG Solar facility in Tomball, Texas

SEG Solar has opened its newest facility, a 4 GW solar module assembly plant in Tomball, Texas. Once the plant is fully operational next year, it will bring SEG’s annual module assembly capacity to 6 GW, joining the company’s original 2 GW facility in nearby Houston.

As part of the grand opening ceremonies, SEG also announced plans to build an additional 4.6 GW module assembly factory within 18 months. The new facility would be located across the street from the new Tomball plant and bring the company’s total annual capacity to 10.6 GW, making it the largest crystalline silicon solar module assembler in the United States. [...] Zhuge closed his portion of the event by displaying a slide with a timeline that extended to 2029, with a photograph of the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City and a heading that read “IPO?”

Following Zhuge’s speech, all the speakers gathered on stage to officially open the plant with a ceremonial switch-throwing, and the company welcomed guests on a tour of the facility.

Plans for operation and employment

During the tour, SEG operations VP Johnson led a group of attendees through the facility, walking step-by-step through the manufacturing lines.

The plant is made with three front-end lines, consisting of cell-stringing and glass and encapsulant layup machines; eight giant lamination machines; and four output lines. [...] “We’re all looking to Jim to pull a rabbit out of the hat, and tell us how we’re going to navigate this next challenge for the solar industry,” Eden said.

The ceremony included numerous speakers in addition to Eden and Wood, including SEG VP of operations Timothy Johnson, senior VP of DEPCOM Power Natasha Cherenkova, Paul Wormser of Intertek CEA, Nico Johnson of Suncast Media and local business leaders.

The final presentation of the event was given by SEG founder and COO Jun Zhuge, who unveiled the company’s plans for expanding its stateside module assembly and cell manufacturing capacity. Zhuge said the company’s U.S. facilities would reach a production level of 70,000 modules a day when the second Tomball factory added 4.6 GW of new capacity in 2027.

Building on the success of its first 2 GW solar module factory, this expansion will increase SEG’s total annual U.S. module production capacity to approximately 6 GW. Commercial operations at the new facility are expected to commence in Q3 2026. [...] The announcement follows SEG’s previously disclosed plan to develop a 5 GW ingot and wafer manufacturing facility in Indonesia, which is expected to begin construction in Q2 2026. Once completed, SEG will be positioned to deliver modules through a fully integrated supply chain spanning ingots, wafers and cells — an increasingly important capability in today’s evolving policy and trade environment. SEG has been validated as a non-PFE for FEOC compliance purposes by multiple independent third parties and currently provides modules with non-PFE solar cells.

About SEG Solar [...] About SEG Solar

Founded in 2021, SEG is a leading vertically integrated PV manufacturer headquartered in Houston, Texas, U.S., and is dedicated to delivering reliable and cost-effective solar modules to the utility, commercial, and residential markets. By the end of 2025, SEG had shipped over 7.5 GW of solar modules worldwide and have achieved a module production capacity of 6.5 GW.

# SEG Solar opens second PV module factory, lifting US capacity to 6GW

Tomball #1 was inaugurated at an event attended by about 800 people. Credit: SEG Solar. · Power Technology · SEG Solar.

Shree Mishra

2 min read

SEG Solar has launched its second photovoltaic (PV) module manufacturing facility in Greater Houston, Texas, expanding its total US production capacity to 6GW per year.

The new plant, Tomball #1, was inaugurated at an event attended by about 800 people, including company staff, local government officials, partners, customers, and media representatives.

The facility represents an investment of $200m and covers more than 500,000ft², making it the company's largest module manufacturing site in the US. [...] "Looking ahead, we are advancing our third US HJT module manufacturing facility and planning a US cell manufacturing facility to build a more integrated domestic supply chain, strengthen long-term delivery capabilities for our customers and establish SEG as the largest crystalline solar module manufacturer in the US."

SEG Solar was founded in 2021 and is based in Houston, Texas.

The company's goal is to deliver solar modules to utility, commercial, and residential markets.

By the end of 2025, SEG Solar had shipped more than 7.5GW of solar modules worldwide and had reached a total production capacity of 6.5GW.

"SEG Solar opens second PV module factory, lifting US capacity to 6GW" was originally created and published by Power Technology, a GlobalData owned brand.
